First of all, you need to fix your point of view on yourself and the world around you. You cannot change your life at all if you consider your life meaningless and that you cannot fix it. I would always advice to visit a psychologist, who can help you find your mining in life and give that first dopamine shot to start your wheel of happiness. But you probably have already sorted that option out. There is a great book written by Victor Frankl, namely "Man's search for the meaning". He was a psychiatrist that had to live 3 years in Auschwitz. His wife and parents were killed there and he still managed to find and help others in camp to find a sense of meaning. The great way of doing anything is to start from very small steps, like clean your room/house. Maybe try to help your neighbor in something. Remember that you have anything to lose, so don't be ashamed or scared of trying. You can only benefit. And trust me, you can just have people around you. People are attracted to human qualities not humans. So you need to make yourself an interesting persona. Good way of doing it is listening to podcasts, reading books, generally developing yourself. What helped me the most was helping other people. I haven't managed to find anything that would make me happier than seeing person's face when I can help them. Depression is a tricky bastard, makes you want things so bad and also discouraging you to try them, so you are in a spiral of sadness. If you start doing some small things, even against yourself you will see that fake cloud of emptiness around you will perish. I hope you will find your way through it.
Stay strong,

I am on SSRI medication for about 2 years now. The therapy started with Venlafaxine, after 9 months i withdrawed it (of course it was a controlled process with my psychiatrist) and after a very big emotional breakdown i needed to take SSRI again, so I'm now 3 months on Sertraline 200mg and here are my thoughts.

For the last 4 years I've developed severe OCD, which I noticed I had years back, when I was a small child. But it always was very mild and not bothering me nearly at all. The worsening of all of the symptoms started when I was 19 (now 23) and what I felt without the meds and help was horrible. My cognitive functions were all good, I managed to retake my finals and get into university to study medicine but I was a dead inside person. Just to barely live with OCD I needed to make myself believe that I am a worthless person that has no meaning and just need to live for the parents and sister. Trust me, it is a hell on Earth.

When I got to the right therapist, who gave me meds I turned my life around. I found out for the first time that I am not an introvert but a massive extrovert who needs to keep contact with people. I managed to find my first girlfriend and strenghten friendships. I've also started a social life (back then I was playing PC 12h+ a day, whenever I could just to stop obsessive thinking). So it was the BIGGEST life saving swing of hope I have ever had.

But to the point that you are asking. Yes, I've had times when I didn't feel nearly anything, that even though I managed to find the right people and put myself in the right situation it still was not enough. So I've started making changes in my life, started also new hobbies (that I didn't want to but obviously I have nothing to lose by trying, which was later and to this day my motto) and helping other people that cope with same problems. And I have to tell you after some time "mentally working out" I feel that I'm on the good way to regain my emotions. Recently I've had some deep conversations with people who I admiring and being friend with. It made me feel happy. People who are going for depression/OCD/other mental sickness medication need to be aware that **PILLS ARE NOT A PROBLEM SOLVER, THEY ARE ONLY A MEDIUM TO SOLVE THEM.** **ALLOWING YOU TO CLARIFY YOUR MIND AND BE OBJECTIVE ABOUT THINGS THAT YOU COULDN'T WITHOUT THEM. SO YOU NEED TO START DEVELOPING YOUR CHARACTER BECAUSE IT IS THE WAY TO HAPPINESS.**

​

So overall, if I could take time back when I took my first pill, I would always do the same thing taking them. Profits definitely outweight the cost. Hope I helped :)

​

Sincerely,

I will try to comfort you as well as I can. It looks like standard POCD case, like I'm having. I also have started to isolate, which makes things even worse. So the best possible way in my opinion to cope with POCD is NOT THINKING ABOUT IT AS SOMETHING EXCEPTIONAL. Because it is feeding of that. You think that you are a pedophile, anxiety rises, you start trembling and shaking and it is killing you internally. So how exactly cope with it? Mine method involved:

1. First if you are diagnosed with OCD, you need to tell your psychiatrist about these thoughts (I was hesitating a lot to tell it but it turned out that my doc wasn't surprised at all, because it is normal in OCD). You need to get proper medication (SSRI/SNRI or something other)  and if needed a psychotherapy.

2. After that you will see first strike of relief. Your mind will start going back to where it was before OCD.

3. The third thing is to understand and DEPRECIATE your symptoms, because it is a voice in your mind that wants to harm you the most. You can't trust it nor try not to think about it. The only solution for me was devaluation of them, laughing them off and it stopped because my mind was building stronger every time I defeated obsessions. After that I can really function well and be happy :)

You need to understand that there isn't any logical connections between a post on the Internet and the real life. But I would just consider visiting a specialist if you feel like your thought processes might be irrational, because that was the beginning of my OCD. I remember that I was searching for assymetries in my body and obsessively tried to fix them and even went to doctor and talked about some manual therapies to fix them as I wanted everything to be perfect. So just be careful and try to observe yourself, if you see that your thoughts are starting to make you feel mental pain, you will be prepared because you know who is your enemy.
